beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: You think Zuckerberg lives on his salary? Here's why he doesn't need to.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: His base salary was $1, for a whole year of running one of the biggest companies on Earth. So where does the real money of the richest come from?

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: A salary that won't even buy a coffee? So what do the richest live on?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: For the richest, wealth isn't a paycheck. It's shares in their companies, which grow with them.

actions.name: Unrealized gain
actions.line: A rise in value you haven't sold

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And in America, shares that rise aren't taxed as income until they're sold.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: But if they don't sell, how do they pay for the jets and the houses?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The richest can borrow against their shares. A loan isn't income, so there's no income tax.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Here's the twist. The 25 richest Americans grew $401B richer in 5 years, and paid $13.6B in federal income tax.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: That's why a paycheck barely matters to them. Shares grow untaxed until sold, loans aren't income, and for those richest Americans, the true tax rate was 3.4%.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: And a paycheck is taxed every payday. So who pays the higher rate, you or them?
